title: Vagus nerve stimulation exerts disease-modifying effects in epileptic rats by enhancing hippocampal adenosine signalling
title_zh: 迷走神经刺激通过增强海马腺苷信号在癫痫大鼠中发挥疾病修饰作用
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) is an established neuromodulatory therapy for refractory epilepsy, but its disease-modifying mechanisms remain unclear. Adenosine is an endogenous anticonvulsant and a key regulator of epileptogenesis, and adenosine kinase (ADK) controls extracellular adenosine availability. This study investigated whether VNS modifies epilepsy progression by regulating hippocampal adenosine signalling. METHODS: A pilocarpine-induced rat model of temporal lobe epilepsy was used. Animals were assigned to control, pilocarpine, VNS-treated, VNS 4-4W (4 weeks of active VNS followed by 4 weeks without stimulation), and sham groups. Spontaneous recurrent seizures (SRS) were monitored using video-electroencephalography, and spatial learning and memory were assessed using the Morris water maze. Hippocampal extracellular adenosine dynamics were measured in vivo using the GRABAdo1.0 sensor combined with fibre photometry. ADK and adenosine A1 receptor (A1R) expression levels were evaluated by immunostaining and Western blotting. RESULTS: Acute VNS induced a rapid increase in hippocampal extracellular adenosine levels. In pilocarpine-treated rats, active VNS significantly reduced the frequency and duration of SRS and improved spatial learning and memory compared with time-matched epileptic rats that did not receive active stimulation. These beneficial effects persisted after a 4-week stimulation-free period. VNS also suppressed hippocampal ADK overexpression and restored A1R expression. Furthermore, pharmacological blockade of A1Rs with DPCPX reversed the antiseizure effect of VNS. CONCLUSIONS: VNS exerts disease-modifying effects in epileptic rats by enhancing hippocampal adenosine signalling. These effects are associated with VNS-evoked adenosine release, inhibition of ADK overexpression, and restoration of A1R-mediated anticonvulsant signalling.
abstract_zh: 目标：迷走神经刺激（VNS）是治疗难治性癫痫的已确立的神经调节疗法，但其疾病修饰机制尚不清楚。腺苷是内源性抗惊厥剂，也是癫痫发生的关键调节因子，腺苷激酶（ADK）控制细胞外腺苷的可用性。本研究探讨VNS是否通过调节海马腺苷信号来改变癫痫进程。方法：采用皮洛卡品诱导的海马癫痫大鼠模型。动物分为对照组、皮洛卡品组、VNS处理组、VNS 4-4W组（4 周主动刺激后 4 周无刺激）和假刺激组。使用视频-脑电图监测自发复发性癫痫发作（SRS），并用 Morris 水迷宫评估空间学习与记忆。通过 GRABAdo1.0 传感器与光纤光度计结合，实时测量海马细胞外腺苷动力学。通过免疫染色和蛋白印迹检测 ADK 与腺苷 A1 受体（A1R）的表达水平。结果：急性 VNS 迅速提高海马细胞外腺苷水平。在皮洛卡品处理的大鼠中，主动 VNS 显著降低 SRS 的频率和持续时间，并改善空间学习与记忆，优于未接受主动刺激的时间匹配癫痫大鼠。这些益处在 4 周无刺激期后仍然存在。VNS 还抑制了海马 ADK 的过度表达并恢复了 A1R 的表达。进一步地，用 DPCPX 阻断 A1R 的药理学抑制逆转了 VNS 的抗惊厥效应。结论：VNS 通过增强海马腺苷信号在癫痫大鼠中发挥疾病修饰作用。这些效应与 VNS 诱导的腺苷释放、ADK 过度表达的抑制以及 A1R 介导的抗惊厥信号的恢复相关。
